reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes Nb reacting with WC in a CoCrFeNi HEA coating to form NbC and improve particle distribution, but it does not involve a W–Cu composite, does not address W/Cu interfaces, and provides no data on interfacial energy, void suppression, phase separation, or thermal conductivity. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Nb segregates to W/Cu interfaces during high-temperature consolidation
Nb reacts in situ to form a stabilizing Nb-rich interphase at W/Cu interfaces
The Nb-rich interphase lowers interfacial energy and suppresses void nucleation
The interphase stabilizes microstructure against phase separation under thermal and irradiation stresses
The stabilized microstructure enhances effective thermal conductivity
